A bypass is a way to get around a security check, restriction, or protection.

Bypass authentication means getting into a system without passing the normal login checks.

California other
California is a U.S. state often referenced in technology, privacy, and cybersecurity policy.

The California Privacy Protection Agency is a California government agency that enforces certain consumer privacy laws.
also: CPPA

cambodia other
Cambodia is a country in Southeast Asia that may be mentioned in cyber reports as a victim location, actor location, or operating base.

An Android malware family that steals information from infected mobile devices.
canada
Canada is a North American country often referenced in cybersecurity reporting as a target, regulator, or law-enforcement partner.
Capability concept
A capability is something a person, tool, system, or attacker is able to do.
CAPTCHAs concept
CAPTCHAs are tests websites use to try to tell humans apart from automated bots.
capture concept
A capture is a part of a regular expression that saves matched text so it can be reused or referenced later.

A cybersecurity exercise in which participants solve security puzzles or find hidden flags in a controlled environment.

CERT-UA organization

certificate transparency logs concept

chatgpt

china
China is a country often referenced in cybersecurity reporting involving technology, espionage, regulation, and threat activity.
China-nexus concept
China-nexus describes activity, infrastructure, or actors assessed to have some connection to China.
Chip product
A named AI agent demonstration referenced in security reporting.
cisa organization

Cisco SD-WAN Cloud product
Cisco's cloud-based service for deploying and managing SD-WAN networks.
Cisco SD-WAN Cloud (Cisco Managed) product
A Cisco-managed cloud service for operating SD-WAN networks on behalf of customers.
Cisco SD-WAN Cloud Hosted product
A cloud-hosted Cisco service for managing software-defined wide-area networks.
Cisco SD-WAN vManage product
A Cisco product used to centrally configure and manage software-defined wide-area networks.

Cisco's Technical Assistance Center, which provides technical support to Cisco customers.

Citrix NetScaler ADC product

Citrix NetScaler ADC and Gateway product
Citrix NetScaler ADC and Gateway is a product used to deliver applications and provide secure remote access to corporate systems.
Citrix NetScaler Gateway product

civil society concept
Civil society means non-government groups, charities, activists, researchers, and community organizations that take part in public life.
civilians concept
Civilians are people who are not members of the military or armed forces.
claude-code

A CLI is a text-based way to control a computer or program by typing commands.

ClickFix lures are social-engineering tricks that persuade users to copy and run commands by pretending to fix a computer or browser problem.

A social-engineering technique that tricks people into running harmful commands by presenting them as a fix or verification step.

A technique that shows different web content to different visitors, often hiding malicious pages from security checks.
cloud concept
The cloud is internet-based computing where data and applications run on remote servers instead of only on your own device.
cloud infrastructure concept
Cloud infrastructure is computing infrastructure provided through internet-based services.
cloud services concept
Computing resources—like storage, apps, and networking—delivered over the internet by providers such as AWS, Azure, and Google Cloud.
cloud-based containerized applications concept
These are applications packaged in containers that are designed to run in cloud computing environments.
cloudflare
Cloudflare is a company that provides content delivery, DDoS protection, DNS, and web security services.

A human-verification challenge branded or provided by Cloudflare that is intended to distinguish people from automated bots.
Cloudflare Pages product
Cloudflare Pages is a Cloudflare service for hosting and deploying websites, especially static sites and frontend applications.

cluster concept
A group of connected computers or appliances that work together as one system.
cluster nodes concept
Cluster nodes are individual computers or servers that work together as part of a larger computing cluster.
Clusters concept
Clusters are groups of connected computers or nodes that work together as one system.
code execution technique
Code execution means an attacker can make a computer or server run commands or software of their choosing.
Code repositories concept
Code repositories are storage locations where software source code and its change history are kept.
code review technique
Code review is the practice of having people or tools examine software code to find mistakes, security issues, or quality problems.
codex
Codex is an OpenAI AI coding model or coding assistant technology for helping write and understand code.
coding concept
Coding is writing instructions in a programming language so a computer can perform tasks.
Coding agents tool
Coding agents are AI tools that can help write, edit, test, or reason about software code.
Cohesity organization
A company that provides data backup, recovery, and security products.
Cohesity Data Cloud product
Cohesity's platform for managing, protecting, and recovering data across different environments.
COLDRIVER threat-actor

Collaboration concept
Collaboration means people or organizations working together, often by sharing information, systems, or responsibilities.
colombia other
Colombia is a country in South America that may be referenced as a location for cyber incidents or targets.
also: Colombian
command execution technique
Command execution means making a computer or device run instructions, often through a shell or remote interface.
command server tool
A command server is an attacker-controlled system that sends instructions to malware or compromised devices.
command-and-control concept
Command-and-control is the way attackers remotely send instructions to malware and receive data back from infected machines.

command-and-control infrastructure concept
Command-and-control infrastructure is the servers and systems attackers use to send instructions to malware and receive stolen data.
Command-and-control server concept
Remote computers controlled by attackers that send orders to infected devices and collect stolen data.
Command-and-control traffic technique
Command-and-control traffic is communication between malware on a victim system and the attacker’s server.
Complete control concept
Complete control means an attacker can fully manage a system, account, or application as if they owned it.
compose.yaml concept

compromise concept

compromised concept
Compromised means a system, account, or device has been accessed or controlled by someone who should not have access.
compromised account concept
An account whose credentials have been stolen or guessed, allowing an attacker to impersonate the legitimate user.
compromised accounts concept
Compromised accounts are user accounts that attackers have gained access to without permission.

A compromised server is a computer system that an attacker has broken into or taken control of.
compromised websites concept

configurable storage locations concept

configuration files concept
Configuration files are files that store settings telling software or systems how to behave.

Connecting concept
Connecting is a status meaning a device, app, or service is trying to establish a network connection.
ConnectWise organization
ConnectWise is a software vendor known for remote management and IT service provider tools.
ConnectWise ScreenConnect product
ConnectWise ScreenConnect is a remote access and support product used to connect to and control computers over the internet.
Consecutive Tour Policy concept
A consecutive tour policy sets rules for how long personnel can serve in back-to-back assignments.
Consent concept
A person's informed agreement to let an organization collect, use, or share their information.
consent phishing technique
Consent phishing tricks a person into approving a malicious app's request to access their online account.
ConsentFix tool
ConsentFix is a named tool or service referenced in privacy or security reporting, likely related to consent handling.
consumer ISP organization
A consumer ISP is a company that provides internet service to homes and individual customers.
Consumer Reports organization
A nonprofit organization that tests products and publishes consumer research and advice.
container concept

container images concept
Container images are packaged snapshots of an application and its needed files that can be run consistently in container environments.
container registry allow lists technique
Container registry allow lists are administrator-defined lists of approved places from which users may download container images.
also: approved registries
container.exe tool

containers concept
Containers are lightweight packages that run applications with their needed files in isolated environments.
containment technique

continuous concept
In security, continuous means something is monitored or updated all the time instead of only during occasional checks.
Control Networks concept
Networks used to operate industrial equipment, building systems, or other physical processes.
control panel product
A control panel is an interface used to manage settings, accounts, systems, or services.
Control systems concept
Control systems are computers and devices that monitor or operate physical equipment such as machines, valves, or production lines.
cookies concept

copy-and-paste activity concept
Copy-and-paste activity means users moving text or data between apps, which can matter for security if sensitive information is copied into unsafe places.
correlation concept
Correlation means finding connections between separate events, data points, or alerts that may be related.

counterparties concept
The other people or organizations involved in a financial transaction or agreement.
Cozy Bear threat-actor
A widely reported Russia-linked threat-actor group, also known as APT29.

credentials concept

critical infrastructure concept
Critical infrastructure refers to essential systems and services that societies and organizations depend on.

cryptocurrency wallets product

CTF, or capture the flag, is a cybersecurity competition where participants solve hacking and defense challenges.
Current process concept
The current process is the program or running task that is executing at a given moment on a computer.
custom withdrawal tool tool
A custom withdrawal tool is purpose-built software for initiating transfers of funds or cryptocurrency from an account or wallet.
customer data concept
Customer data is information a company keeps about its customers, such as names, contact details, or purchase history.
customer information concept
Customer information is data a business keeps about its customers, such as names, contact details, purchases, or account records.
CVE vulnerability
A CVE is a public identifier used to track a specific known software vulnerability.
CVSS score concept
A CVSS score is a standard number used to show how severe a software vulnerability is.
CVSS score of 9.8 concept
A very high rating on the Common Vulnerability Scoring System, indicating a critical security flaw.
cyber concept
Cyber is a broad shorthand for things related to computers, networks, and digital security.
cyber classifiers tool
Cyber classifiers are tools or models that sort security-related data, such as labeling activity as benign or suspicious.
also: OpenAI’s cyber safeguards
Cyber Command 2.0 concept
Cyber Command 2.0 is a name for a modernization effort involving U.S. Cyber Command.
cyber incidents concept
Cyber incidents are events that threaten or harm computer systems, networks, or data.
Cyber Mission Force organization
The main operational workforce of U.S. Cyber Command, made up of teams conducting cyber missions.
also: CMF
Cyber Occupational Resiliency and Engagement Framework concept
The Cyber Occupational Resiliency and Engagement Framework is a planned structure for supporting the well-being and long-term performance of cyber personnel.
Cyber Operators concept
Personnel who conduct or support cybersecurity and computer network operations.
cyber resilience concept
Cyber resilience is an organization's ability to keep operating and recover quickly when cyberattacks or failures happen.
Cyber Talent Management Organization organization
Cyber Talent Management Organization is a U.S. Department of Defense organization focused on cyber workforce hiring and management.
CyberArk organization
CyberArk is a cybersecurity company best known for products that protect privileged accounts, passwords, and secrets.
Cybersecurity concept
Cybersecurity is the practice of protecting computers, networks, software, and data from digital attacks or misuse.
cybersecurity researchers organization
Cybersecurity researchers are people who study digital threats, software flaws, and attacks to help protect systems.
cybersecurity-and-infrastructure-security-agency organization
The Cybersecurity and Infrastructure Security Agency is the U.S. government agency that helps defend critical infrastructure and improve cybersecurity.
Cyberspace concept
Cyberspace is the digital world of computers, networks, online services, and data.
Cyera Research organization
Cyera Research is the security research team associated with the data security company Cyera.
DarkSword malware
DarkSword is a named malware family, threat, or cyber tool referenced in security reporting.
dashboard tool
A dashboard is a visual interface where users manage settings and view information in a product.
Data access concept
Data access means the ability to view, use, change, or retrieve information from a system.
data brokers concept
Data brokers are companies that collect, buy, and sell personal information about people.
data centers concept
Data centers are facilities full of servers and networking equipment that run websites, cloud services, and business systems.
Data collection concept
Data collection is the process of gathering information from people, systems, devices, or services for analysis or use.
data discovery technique
Data discovery is the process of finding where data lives, what it contains, and whether it is sensitive.
data exfiltration technique
Data exfiltration is the unauthorized removal or copying of data from a system.
also: data removal
data leak concept
A data leak is when private or sensitive information is exposed to people who should not have it.
data security concept
Data security is the practice of protecting information from unauthorized access, theft, damage, or exposure.
Data source concept
The system, application, or location from which data originates.
data theft concept
Data theft is the stealing of information from a system or service.
Data transfers concept
Data transfers are movements of information from one person, system, company, or country to another.
Database Connection Strings concept
Settings that tell an application how to connect to a database, sometimes including sensitive login details.
database password concept
A database password is a secret used to prove permission to access a database.
Datagram Transport Layer Security protocol
Datagram Transport Layer Security, or DTLS, is a protocol that encrypts and protects data sent over connectionless networks such as UDP.
DataLock product
A Cohesity data-protection capability that provides immutable storage controls and encryption features.
datasets concept
Datasets are collections of information that researchers or tools analyze to find patterns and evidence.
Dead-Drop C2 technique
A command-and-control technique in which malware exchanges instructions through an indirect shared service, such as a cloud account or web page.
also: Dead-drop C2 communication, dead-drop C2 channels, dead-drop C2 designs
Debian product
A well-known community-driven Linux distribution famous for its stability and package management system.
debugger tool
A debugger is a tool developers and security researchers use to inspect and control how a program runs.
deception technique
Deception is tricking a person or system into believing something false, often to gain access or hide activity.
decoy document technique
A decoy document is a harmless-looking file used to trick a target into opening it while malware or tracking runs in the background.
decryption concept
Decryption is the process of turning scrambled encrypted data back into readable information.
decryption key concept
A decryption key is the secret digital value needed to unlock encrypted files or messages.
Defender product
Defender usually refers to Microsoft Defender, Microsoft’s built-in security and antimalware product line.
defenders concept
Defenders are the people or teams responsible for protecting systems and responding to cyber threats.
Delegated Authorization concept
Delegated authorization lets a user allow an application or device to act with selected permissions on the user's behalf.
delegated permissions concept
Delegated permissions let an app act with the rights of a signed-in user instead of using only its own identity.
denial-of-service
Denial-of-service is an attack that overwhelms a system so legitimate users cannot access it.
denial-of-service condition concept
A denial-of-service condition is a situation where a system becomes unavailable or unusable for legitimate users.
Department of Defense organization
The Department of Defense is the U.S. government department responsible for the military and national defense.
also: DOD
deposit concept
Money paid in advance, often as a requirement before receiving a service or making a purchase.
Detect technique
Detect means to identify suspicious or malicious activity in systems, networks, or data.
detection concept
Detection is the process of finding signs of suspicious or malicious activity.
detections concept
Alerts or findings generated by security tools indicating that a potential threat or malicious activity has been identified.
deterministic tools concept
Deterministic tools are tools that produce the same result every time when given the same input.
developer workflows concept
Developer workflows are the regular steps software developers use to write, test, review, and release code.
Device-code authentication protocol
Device-code authentication is a login method where one device shows a code that the user enters on another device to approve access.
device-code authentication flow protocol
Device-code authentication flow lets a device sign in by showing a code that the user enters on another device or browser.
device-code-phishing technique
Device-code phishing tricks users into entering a legitimate login code that gives attackers access to their account.
device_code protocol
device_code is a code used behind the scenes in OAuth device login to identify the device waiting for user approval.
digital currency concept
Digital currency is money or value that exists electronically rather than as physical cash.
Digital Warfighting Campaigns concept
Digital warfighting campaigns are coordinated military operations conducted through cyberspace and digital systems.
digitally signed concept
Digitally signed means software or data includes a cryptographic stamp meant to prove who created it and whether it was changed.
diplomats other
Diplomats are government representatives who work on international relations and may be cyber targets because they handle sensitive political information.
Disclosure concept
Disclosure is the act of reporting or publishing information about a security issue so it can be understood and fixed.
Disconnect product
Disconnect is likely a product, command, or feature name referenced in a security or privacy context.
Display name concept
A display name is the human-readable name shown for an account, sender, or object, which may differ from its real identifier.
display-name-spoofing technique
Display-name-spoofing is making an email sender name look like a trusted person or company even when the real address is different.
DIVD organization
DIVD, the Dutch Institute for Vulnerability Disclosure, is a Dutch nonprofit organization that helps identify and report security flaws.
DKIM protocol
DKIM is an email signing method that helps verify that a message was authorized by a domain and was not changed after signing.
DLL concept
A DLL is a Windows file that contains code other programs can load and use.
DLL sideloading technique
DLL sideloading is an attack where malware places a fake DLL where a trusted Windows program will load it.
also: DLL-sideloading bundle, Signed-host DLL sideloading
dllhost tool
A legitimate Windows process (dllhost.exe) used for COM operations, often abused by attackers to hide malicious activity in plain sight.
DLLs concept
Dynamic-link library files that contain code and resources programs can share on Windows.
DMARC protocol
DMARC is an email policy check that uses SPF or DKIM alignment to help determine whether a message claiming to come from a domain should be trusted.
DNS protocol
DNS is the internet system that turns human-readable names like example.com into the numeric addresses computers use to find websites and services.
DNS history concept
DNS history shows how a domain name’s internet records have changed over time, such as which IP addresses it pointed to.
DNS-over-HTTPS protocol
DNS-over-HTTPS is a protocol that encrypts DNS lookups by sending them through HTTPS, making browsing requests harder to monitor or tamper with.
Docker Compose tool
Docker Compose is a tool for defining and running multi-container Docker applications from a configuration file.
also: Compose
DocuSign product
A widely used electronic signature and document management service for secure digital agreements.
Domain registration concept
Domain registration is the process of reserving an internet name, such as example.com, so it can be used for a website or email.
downloader malware
A downloader is malware or a small program that retrieves and installs additional malicious code from the internet.
Dropbox product
Dropbox is a cloud storage and file-sharing service.
droppers malware
Droppers are malware programs whose main job is to install or download other malware onto a device.
drug cartels concept
Organized criminal groups that make money by illegally producing, moving, or selling drugs.
also: Colombian and Mexican drug cartels
drug trafficking concept
Drug trafficking is the illegal production, transport, or sale of controlled drugs.
DTLS protocol
DTLS is a security protocol that protects datagram network traffic, similar to how TLS protects web connections.
DTLS fragment reassembly technique
DTLS fragment reassembly is the process of joining pieces of a DTLS handshake message into the original complete message.
DTLS Handshake Header protocol
A header in the setup messages of the Datagram Transport Layer Security protocol that describes information about the message.
Dutch Institute for Vulnerability Disclosure (DIVD) organization
The Dutch Institute for Vulnerability Disclosure, or DIVD, is a Dutch nonprofit organization that helps identify and report security flaws.
Dwell Phasing concept
Dwell phasing is a personnel-planning method that schedules predictable time away from demanding assignments for recovery.
EDR product
EDR is security software that monitors computers and servers for suspicious activity and helps respond to attacks.
ELEVATE technique
ELEVATE is a named privilege-raising or exploitation step referenced in security reporting.
Elevated concept
Elevated means running with higher permissions than a normal user, such as administrator-level access.
elevated privileges concept
Higher access rights than a standard user, allowing actions like installing software or modifying system files.
Elite Performance Modeling concept
Elite performance modeling is an approach that studies high-performing groups to improve training, health, and sustained performance.
email accounts concept
Email accounts are user accounts that let people send, receive, and store email messages.
email address concept
An email address is the unique address used to send messages to someone's email account.
email addresses concept
Email addresses are the unique names people use to send and receive email, such as user@example.com.
email authentication concept
Technical methods that verify an email came from the domain it claims and hasn't been forged.
email campaigns concept
Email campaigns are organized batches of emails sent to many recipients for marketing, communication, or scams.
Email phishing technique
Email phishing is a scam where attackers send deceptive emails to trick people into clicking links, opening files, or giving up information.
embeddings concept
Embeddings are numeric representations of text, images, or other data that let AI systems compare and retrieve similar items.
also: embedding, embedding models
encrypted concept
Encrypted data has been scrambled so that only someone with the right key can read it.
encrypted DNS protocol
Encrypted DNS hides DNS lookups from easy snooping by encrypting the requests that translate names into internet addresses.
encrypted payload concept
Hidden code or data that must be decrypted before it can run or be used.
encryption concept
Encryption is a way of scrambling information so only someone with the right key can read it.
Encryption keys concept
Encryption keys are secret values used to lock and unlock protected data.
endpoint concept
An endpoint is a user device such as a laptop, phone, or server that connects to a network.
endpoints concept
Endpoints are user-facing devices such as laptops, desktops, or phones that connect to systems and data.
engagement concept
Engagement means how often people interact with a website, app, message, or notification.
Enrollment concept
Enrollment is the process of registering a device or user with an organization's management system.
Enterprise Perimeters concept
Enterprise perimeters are the outer boundaries of an organization's network where internet-facing systems are protected and monitored.
Enterprise Search concept
A search capability that lets an organization find information across many internal systems and data stores.
Enterprise services concept
Enterprise services are business IT systems or applications used across an organization.
Entra product
Microsoft Entra is Microsoft’s identity and access management product family, including cloud directory and login services.
Entra Agent ID concept
Entra Agent ID is an identity associated with a Microsoft Entra agent or automation component.
entra-id
Microsoft Entra ID is Microsoft’s cloud identity service, formerly called Azure Active Directory.
also: Entra ID application
entry point concept
An entry point is the place or method an attacker, program, or process first uses to get into a system or workflow.
envelope sender protocol
The envelope sender is the technical return address used during email delivery, which may differ from the visible From address.
environment variable concept
An environment variable is a setting stored by an operating system or application that programs can read while they run.
environment variables concept
Environment variables are named settings stored by an operating system or runtime that programs can read while they run.
Escalation concept
An escalation is a security case passed to a person or higher-level team because it needs additional attention or action.
Espionage Campaign concept
An espionage campaign is a coordinated spying operation intended to gather secret or sensitive information.
eth concept
The standard network interface naming prefix for Ethernet devices in Linux and Unix-like systems.
ethereum
Ethereum is a blockchain platform used for cryptocurrency, smart contracts, and decentralized applications.
EtherHiding technique
EtherHiding is a technique where attackers hide malicious code or instructions in blockchain smart contracts.
europe
Europe is a continent often referenced in cybersecurity reporting involving regulations, victims, threat activity, or law enforcement.
evade detection technique
To evade detection means to hide malicious activity so security tools or analysts do not notice it.
evasion technique
A technique used by attackers to avoid detection by security tools like antivirus or firewalls.
Evilginx tool
Evilginx is a phishing tool that can act as a proxy to steal login sessions and bypass some multi-factor authentication protections.
Exchange Online product
Exchange Online is Microsoft’s cloud-hosted email and calendar service in Microsoft 365.
EXE other
A file extension on Windows that runs an executable program, commonly used to install software but also to deliver malware.
executable concept
An executable is a file that can run as a program on a computer.
executable code concept
Instructions that a computer can run to perform actions.
Execute code concept
Execute code means to make a computer run instructions, which is dangerous if an attacker can run their own code.
Execution technique
Execution is the stage where an attacker runs code or commands on a target system.
exfiltrate email technique
To exfiltrate email means to secretly steal or copy email messages out of an account or mail system.
exfiltrated technique
Exfiltrated means data was secretly copied or moved out of a system by an attacker.
exfiltrated data concept
Exfiltrated data is information that has been secretly stolen or copied out of a system.
exfiltration technique
Exfiltration is the unauthorized removal or theft of data from a system or organization.
Exit Interview concept
An exit interview is a discussion with someone leaving an organization to gather feedback about their experience.
also: standardized exit interview summaries
exploit kit tool
An exploit kit is a package of tools criminals use to automatically find and exploit vulnerable browsers, plugins, or systems.
exploit mechanics concept
Exploit mechanics are the technical details of how an exploit triggers and uses a vulnerability.
Exploit path concept
An exploit path is the chain of steps an attacker could take to reach and abuse a vulnerability.
exploitation technique
Exploitation is taking advantage of a weakness in software or people to gain unauthorized access or control.
Exploited technique
Exploited means attackers successfully took advantage of a weakness in software or a system.
exploited in the wild concept
Exploited in the wild means attackers are actively using a vulnerability against real targets, not just in a lab.
Exploits technique
Exploits are code or techniques that take advantage of software vulnerabilities.
Exposed concept
Accessible in a way that could allow a threat to reach or affect a system.
exposed credentials concept
Login details that have been accidentally published or stolen, granting unauthorized access.
Exposed Enterprise Services concept
Exposed enterprise services are business systems that can be reached from the public internet and may be attacked if not properly secured.
exposed secrets concept
Exposed secrets are leaked passwords, API keys, tokens, or other sensitive credentials that attackers could use.
External script injection technique
External script injection is when an attacker causes a website or application to load and run script code from an outside source.
extortion concept
Extortion is pressuring someone to give up money, data, or something valuable through threats.
also: extortion pressure
Facebook Pixel tool
A Meta tracking code placed on websites to report visitor actions for advertising measurement.
fake accounts technique
Fake accounts are online accounts created with false identities, often used for spam, scams, manipulation, or evasion.
fake GitHub identities technique
Fake GitHub identities are made-up or impersonated accounts used to appear trustworthy on the GitHub code-sharing platform.
also: new account, one identity, another account
fake-captcha
A fake CAPTCHA is a deceptive “prove you are human” prompt that tricks users into running commands or installing malware.
false positives concept
False positives are alerts that incorrectly label harmless activity as suspicious or malicious.
Faronics Deploy Agent product
A legitimate Faronics software-deployment tool used to install and manage software on endpoint devices.
Favicon Hashes concept
Short identifiers calculated from a website's browser icon that can help researchers recognize related websites or servers.
fbi organization
The FBI is the U.S. Federal Bureau of Investigation, which investigates cybercrime and national security threats.
also: FBI officials
FBI’s Ten Most Wanted Fugitives List product
The FBI's public list of people it considers especially important fugitives to locate and arrest.
also: FBI’s most wanted list
Federal Bureau of Investigation organization
The Federal Bureau of Investigation is the main U.S. federal law-enforcement agency that investigates crimes including cybercrime.
Federal Trade Commission organization
The Federal Trade Commission is a United States government agency that handles consumer protection issues.
also: FTC
few-shot prompting technique
Few-shot prompting gives an AI model a small number of examples to show it how to answer a task.
file encryption concept
File encryption scrambles files so they cannot be read without the right key or password.
File Extensions concept
The letters after a file name's final period that usually indicate its format, such as .pdf or .exe.
file storage concept
File storage is space for saving and retrieving digital documents, images, and other files.
final payload concept
A final payload is the main malicious program or action delivered after earlier stages prepare the target system.
financial fraud concept
Financial fraud is deception used to steal money or gain an improper financial benefit.
financial institutions organization
Financial institutions are organizations such as banks, credit unions, insurers, and investment firms that handle money and financial services.
financial sector concept
The financial sector includes organizations and services involved in money, banking, investments, and payments.
financial services organization
Financial services are businesses such as banks, payment companies, insurers, and investment firms that manage money or financial transactions.
fingerprints concept
Fingerprints are unique identifying clues, such as file hashes or device traits, that help recognize a person, system, or file.
FIPS concept
FIPS are U.S. government standards for federal computer systems, including rules for approved cryptography.
FIPS-Compliant Encryption concept
Encryption that meets U.S. Federal Information Processing Standards requirements.
Firewall rule concept
A firewall rule is an instruction that allows, blocks, or limits network traffic.
First-Time Sender concept
A sender-history signal that checks whether an email sender has contacted a recipient before.
flaw concept
A flaw is a weakness or mistake in software, design, or configuration that can cause problems or security risk.
Folder concept
A Folder is a container used to organize related files, tasks, lists, or projects in a computer or app.
folders concept
Folders are containers used to organize files in a computer system.
Force Employment concept
Force employment is the planning and use of military personnel and units to carry out missions.
foreign adversaries concept
Foreign adversaries are governments or groups from other countries that may try to spy on, disrupt, or attack systems.
Fort Meade organization
Fort Meade is a U.S. military installation in Maryland associated with agencies such as the National Security Agency and U.S. Cyber Command.
Fragment concept
A fragment is a smaller piece of data, code, or a URL that forms part of a larger item.
fragment_length Field concept
A protocol field that states how large an individual piece of a split message is supposed to be.
also: fragment\_length
Fragments concept
Fragments are smaller pieces of a larger network message that are sent separately and later put back together.
france other
France is a country in Western Europe.
fraud concept
Fraud is dishonest activity intended to trick someone for money, access, or other benefit.
freebsd
FreeBSD is a Unix-like open-source operating system often used for servers and networking.
FSB organization
FSB is Russia's Federal Security Service, an intelligence and security agency often referenced in cyber-espionage reporting.
Fully Hydrated Snapshots concept
Complete saved copies of data that are ready to restore without needing to rebuild missing parts first.
Gap organization
Gap is a clothing and retail company.
gateway product
A gateway is a system that sits between networks or services and controls or forwards traffic.
gather intelligence technique
To gather intelligence means to collect information that helps understand a target, threat, or situation.
GatherOsState.exe tool
A legitimate Microsoft-signed Windows executable that collects operating-system information for deployment or compatibility tools.
General availability concept
General availability means a product or feature is officially released for normal customer use.
General Motors organization
General Motors is a U.S. automobile manufacturer that owns brands including Chevrolet, GMC, Buick, and Cadillac.
also: GM
Ghidra tool
Ghidra is a free reverse-engineering tool from the U.S. National Security Agency used to analyze compiled software and malware.
gists product
Gists are GitHub-hosted snippets of code, notes, or text that can be shared publicly or privately.
GitHub product
GitHub is a platform for storing, managing, and collaborating on software code.
GitHub accounts product
GitHub accounts are user accounts on GitHub used to host code, collaborate on software, and manage development projects.
GitHub CLI tool
GitHub CLI is a command-line tool for working with GitHub from a terminal.
GitHub Enterprise Cloud product
GitHub Enterprise Cloud is GitHub's hosted business version for managing private code repositories and collaboration at scale.
GitHub Issues product
GitHub Issues is GitHub's feature for tracking bugs, tasks, questions, and discussions about software projects.
also: issue
GitHub organization product
A GitHub organization is a shared GitHub account that lets a company or group manage members and code repositories together.
GitHub Push Protection product
GitHub Push Protection is a feature that warns or blocks users from pushing detected secrets, such as access tokens, to repositories.
GitHub repositories product
GitHub repositories are online project folders on GitHub where source code and related files are stored.
GitHub repository tool
A GitHub repository is an online project folder on GitHub that stores code, files, history, and collaboration settings.
github-release-assets other
github-release-assets is a term associated with GitHub release attachments, which are files published alongside software releases.
GitLab product
GitLab is a platform for hosting source code, managing software development, and running CI/CD pipelines.
gitshot tool
gitshot is an open-source tool for uploading screenshots to GitHub for use in code reviews and discussions.
Glow organization
Glow is a security company referenced in security reporting.
Gmail product
Gmail is Google’s email service.
Google organization
Google is a technology company that provides online services, including email-related services.
Google API keys concept
Google API keys are credentials that let an application access Google services and APIs.
Google Cloud product
Google's suite of cloud computing services offering infrastructure, platform, and machine learning capabilities.
Google Cloud Service Account Credentials concept
Google Cloud service account credentials are keys or files that allow software to authenticate to Google Cloud services without a human signing in.
Google Meet product
Google Meet is Google's video conferencing service for online meetings and calls.
Google researchers organization
Security researchers who work for Google and investigate digital threats and vulnerabilities.
Google Search product
Google Search is Google's web search engine for finding information online.
Google Sites product
Google Sites is Google's website-building service for creating simple web pages.
Google's Threat Intelligence Group organization
Google's Threat Intelligence Group is a Google security team that researches cyber threats, attackers, and major security incidents.
also: GTIG
google-threat-intelligence-group
Google Threat Intelligence Group is Google’s team that analyzes cyber threats and shares intelligence about attackers and malware.
google-workspace
Google Workspace is Google’s cloud productivity suite, including Gmail, Drive, Docs, and Calendar for organizations.
governance concept
Governance is the set of rules, oversight, and decision-making processes used to manage an organization or technology safely.
Governance and Cyber Wellness Working Group organization
The Governance and Cyber Wellness Working Group is a group formed to coordinate policy and support for cyber personnel well-being.
government websites concept
Government websites are official online sites run by public agencies or state institutions.
GPT-5.5 product
An unreleased or speculative intermediate version of OpenAI's Generative Pre-trained Transformer model, expected to bridge capabilities between GPT-5 and GPT-6.
GPT-5.6 Sol product
GPT-5.6 Sol is a named AI model or model variant referenced in security reporting.
gpt-6-astra product
gpt-6-astra is a named AI-related model, package, or benchmark identifier referenced in security reporting.
also: The model
graph concept
A graph is a way to show connected things, such as computers, users, applications, and the relationships between them.
GreyNoise organization
GreyNoise is a cybersecurity company that tracks and labels internet scanning and attack activity.
hackers concept
Individuals who use technical skills to gain unauthorized access to computer systems, or security researchers who test defenses.
hacking concept
Hacking is gaining access to or interfering with computer systems or data without permission.
Hacktron organization
A security research firm referenced in reporting.
Hacktron AI tool
Hacktron AI is an automated security research system referenced in security reporting.
handshake protocol
A handshake is the initial exchange where two systems agree how to communicate securely or reliably.
handshake message protocol
A setup message exchanged between systems to establish a secure network connection.
HARM tool
An agentic AI red-teaming framework used to generate and evaluate jailbreak and multi-turn attacks.
Harness tool
A harness is a testing setup that runs software or code in a controlled way so researchers can observe how it behaves.
health checks concept
Health checks are automated tests that determine whether an application or container is running properly.
heap concept
The heap is an area of computer memory that programs use to store data while they are running.
Heap memory concept
Heap memory is a part of a program's memory used for data that is created and managed while the program runs.
heap-based-buffer-overflow
A heap-based buffer overflow is a memory bug where a program writes too much data into heap memory, possibly allowing code execution.
Hell's Gate technique
A Windows evasion technique that makes system calls directly to avoid security software that watches normal API functions.
helpdesk organization
A helpdesk is a support team that helps users with account, computer, and access problems.
high severity concept
High severity means a security issue is considered serious and should usually be fixed quickly.
high-risk vulnerabilities vulnerability
High-risk vulnerabilities are software flaws considered likely to cause serious harm if attackers exploit them.
also: high-severity flaws
High-severity vulnerabilities vulnerability
High-severity vulnerabilities are serious software weaknesses that could cause major security harm if exploited.
High-tempo cyber operations concept
Cyber missions conducted at a fast, sustained pace that can place heavy demands on personnel.
hijack sessions technique
To hijack sessions means to take over someone’s logged-in web or app session so the attacker can act as that user.
hijacking technique
Hijacking in cybersecurity means taking control of something, such as a browser session, account, or network setting, without permission.
Hit-and-Run technique
An attack style in which attackers quickly steal data or cause harm and then leave to reduce the chance of being detected.
HKCU Run technique
A Windows Registry startup location that can make a program run automatically whenever the current user signs in.
also: Registry Run value, Run key
Honda organization
Honda is a Japanese company that makes automobiles, motorcycles, and other products.
Hooks concept
Hooks are points where software can run custom code when certain events happen.
hosted concept
Hosted means a service, website, or system is running on someone’s server so other people can access it.
hosting patterns concept
Hosting patterns are recurring ways that online systems are hosted or arranged.
Hot and Warm Wallets concept
Cryptocurrency wallets that are connected to systems often enough to support routine transfers, making them more accessible than cold wallets.
HTA product
HTA is a Microsoft HTML Application file type that can run scripts and has often been abused to launch malware on Windows.
also: HTA stager, HTA-hosted JScript downloader and decryptor
HTML Content concept
The code and text that make up the structure and content of a web page.
HTTP protocol
HTTP is a common way for computers to send web requests and responses over a network.
HTTP 404 responses protocol
Web-server replies saying that the requested page or resource could not be found.
HTTP headers protocol
HTTP headers are extra pieces of information sent with web requests and responses, such as browser type, cookies, or content format.
HTTP POST requests protocol
HTTP POST requests are web requests commonly used to send data, such as form submissions, to a server.
HTTP requests protocol
HTTP requests are messages a browser or app sends to a web server to ask for a page, file, or action.
HTTPS protocol
HTTPS is the secure version of the web protocol used to protect data sent between your browser and a website.
Hugging Face organization
Hugging Face is a company and platform for sharing machine learning models, datasets, and AI tools.
human resources organization
Human resources is the part of an organization that handles employee records, hiring, benefits, and workplace policies.
Hunt technique
Hunt means to proactively search systems and networks for signs of hidden threats or attacker activity.
huntress organization
Huntress is a cybersecurity company providing managed detection and response for small and midsize organizations.
Hyper-V product
Hyper-V is Microsoft's virtualization product for running virtual machines on Windows systems.
ICO organization
ICO is the abbreviation used in the article for the UK information regulator whose work Edwards said he did not want to distract from.
identities concept
Identities are accounts or actors that systems recognize and allow to access resources.
Identity management concept
Identity management is the process of creating, controlling, and securing user and service accounts.

impersonate technique

impersonation technique

in memory concept

inbound concept

Incident investigation is the process of figuring out what happened during a security event and how to fix it.

incident response concept

incidents concept

india

indicator concept

indicators concept

infect concept

intelligence collection concept

investigation concept
