OpenSSL 3.6.5 product
A version of OpenSSL, a widely used software library for encrypting network communications.
OpenSSL 4.0.3 product
A version of OpenSSL, a widely used software library for encrypting network communications.
OpenSSL Project organization
The OpenSSL Project is the organization that develops and maintains OpenSSL, a widely used toolkit for encrypted communications.
Operating system concept
An operating system is the main software that manages a computer or phone, such as Windows, macOS, Android, or iOS.
Operating systems product
Core software that manages a computer's hardware and lets applications run.
Operation Epic Fury concept
Operation Epic Fury is a named military operation referenced in reporting.
Operational Restitution concept
Operational restitution is time and support intended to help personnel recover after intensive work or deployments.
also: reconstitution between deployments
Operator tool
An Operator is a Kubernetes automation component that manages an application by encoding operational tasks into software.
operators concept
Operators are the people or groups running a system, service, campaign, or criminal operation.
Optimism product
A blockchain network designed to process Ethereum-related transactions more cheaply and quickly.
Optimized Unit Phasing concept
Optimized unit phasing is an approach to scheduling teams so people can balance operational work with rest and recovery.
OR-Tools tool
Google's open-source software suite for mathematical optimization and operations research problems.
oracle
Oracle is a technology company known for databases, enterprise software, cloud services, and Java-related products.
Organizational Climate Survey concept
An organizational climate survey is a questionnaire used to measure employees' views about their workplace culture and conditions.
also: organizational climate survey data
Outdated concept
Outdated means software, data, or settings are old and may be missing important fixes or protections.
Outlook product
Outlook is Microsoft's email and calendar application used by individuals and organizations.
also: Outlook mailbox
oversight concept
Oversight means watching over an activity or organization to make sure rules are followed and problems are caught.
pace concept
Pace is the speed or rhythm of speech, movement, or activity and can be used as a behavior signal.
package ecosystem concept
A package ecosystem is a community and registry where developers publish and download reusable software libraries.
package versions concept
Package versions are numbered releases of software components that help track updates and fixes.
Packet concept
A packet is a small chunk of data sent across a network.
Parallels organization
A software company known for virtualization products, including Parallels Desktop.
passive DNS technique
Passive DNS is a way of collecting historical DNS lookup data to see which domains pointed to which internet addresses over time.
Passkeys concept
Passkeys are a newer way to sign in using your device or biometrics instead of typing a password.
password-protected archive concept
A password-protected archive is a compressed file, such as a ZIP, that requires a password to open and is sometimes used to hide malicious files from scanners.
Password-Protected ZIP concept
A ZIP archive that requires a password before its contents can be opened.
patched concept
Patched means a software flaw has been fixed with an update.
patches concept
Patches are software updates that fix bugs, security flaws, or other problems.
patching concept
Applying software updates to fix security holes and bugs.
path traversal flaw vulnerability
A path traversal flaw is a weakness that lets someone reach files or locations outside the intended area.
path-traversal vulnerability
Path traversal is a vulnerability where attackers use file path tricks to access files they should not be able to reach.
payload concept
A payload is the part of malicious code that performs the attacker’s intended action.
Payload Delivery Stage technique
The point in an attack when malicious code or files are sent to the intended target.
payloads concept
Payloads are the parts of malware or an exploit that perform the attacker's intended action, such as stealing data or installing ransomware.
Pentagon organization
The Pentagon is the headquarters of the U.S. Department of Defense and is often used to refer to that department.
perimeter concept
A perimeter is the boundary between an organization's internal network and outside networks such as the internet.
Perimeter Appliances product
Perimeter appliances are network devices, such as firewalls and VPN gateways, that sit at the edge of an organization's network.
also: edge and security appliances
Permissions Structure concept
The arrangement of rules that determines which users or groups can access particular data and systems.
persistence concept
Persistence is the ability for an attacker to keep access to a system over time.
Persistence mechanisms technique
Persistence mechanisms are ways attackers keep access to a system even after restarts, password changes, or cleanup attempts.
persistent access concept
Persistent access means continued access to an account or system over time.
Persistent remote access technique
Persistent remote access means an attacker keeps a way to reconnect to a system even after reboots or temporary disruptions.
personal information concept
Personal information is data that can identify or describe a person, such as a name, address, phone number, or account details.
Personally identifiable data concept
Personally identifiable data is information that can identify a specific person, such as a name, address, ID number, or email address.
also: private data, personal data
personally identifiable information concept
Personally identifiable information is data that can identify a person, such as a name, address, Social Security number, or email address.
philippines other
The Philippines is a country in Southeast Asia that may be mentioned in cyber reports as a victim location, actor location, or operating base.
phishing technique
Phishing is a scam where attackers impersonate trusted people or services to steal information or make victims take unsafe actions.
phishing campaign technique
A phishing campaign is a coordinated effort to trick people into giving up passwords, money, or other sensitive information.
phishing campaigns technique
Phishing campaigns are organized attempts to trick many people into revealing information or installing malware using fake messages.
phishing chain concept
A phishing chain is the series of steps attackers use to trick someone, such as an email, a link, a fake page, and a final payload.
Phishing delivery technique
Phishing delivery is the way a scam message or malicious link is sent to a target, such as by email, text, or phone.
phishing domains concept
Phishing domains are website names registered or used to trick people into trusting fake sites.
phishing email technique
A phishing email is a fake or deceptive message designed to trick someone into revealing information or clicking something harmful.
phishing emails technique
Phishing emails are fake messages designed to trick people into revealing information or clicking harmful links.
Phishing kits tool
Phishing kits are ready-made tools criminals use to create fake login pages and steal credentials.
phishing links technique
Phishing links are deceptive web links that try to trick people into giving away passwords, money, or sensitive information.
Phishing lure technique
A phishing lure is the fake message, link, or story used to trick someone into clicking or sharing information.
phishing pages technique
Phishing pages are fake web pages designed to trick people into entering passwords, codes, or other sensitive information.
phishing-resistant sign-in technique
Phishing-resistant sign-in uses login methods, such as hardware security keys or passkeys, that are hard for fake websites to trick.
phone numbers concept
Phone numbers are the unique numbers used to reach people or devices on telephone networks.
PHP web shell malware
A PHP web shell is a malicious script uploaded to a web server that lets an attacker run commands through a browser.
PHP web shells tool
PHP web shells are small scripts attackers place on a web server so they can run commands through a browser.
PII concept
PII means personally identifiable information, such as names, addresses, ID numbers, or other data that can identify a person.
Pinterest organization
Pinterest is an online platform where people save and share images, ideas, and links.
Ploutus malware
A malware family designed to make automated teller machines dispense cash illegally.
also: Ploutus malware
Plus 5.6 product
A named custom GPT referenced in security reporting.
poland other
Poland is a country in Europe.
Port 48678 protocol
A numbered network communication endpoint used by a service to receive connections.
postinstall technique
postinstall is a package script that runs automatically after software is installed, often in npm packages.
powershell
PowerShell is Microsoft’s command-line shell and scripting language, often used by administrators and abused by attackers.
also: powershell.exe, PowerShell execution
pre-authentication concept
Pre-authentication means something happens before a user has logged in or proven who they are.
also: pre-auth
Pre-Authentication Integer Underflow vulnerability
A software error where a number becomes smaller than its allowed range before login checks occur, potentially enabling an attack.
pre-authentication remote code execution vulnerability
Pre-authentication remote code execution is a serious flaw that lets an attacker run code on a system from afar without needing to log in first.
Precise concept
Carefully targeted and intended to avoid unnecessary effects.
Precise Geolocations concept
Precise geolocations are highly accurate estimates of a device's physical location, often based on GPS or nearby networks.
also: ingested location data
Preservation of the Force and Family concept
Preservation of the Force and Family is a U.S. Special Operations Command program focused on service members' health, readiness, and family well-being.
Private information concept
Private information is personal or confidential data that should not be shared without permission.
privilege-escalation technique
Privilege escalation is when an attacker gains higher levels of access than they were supposed to have.
privileged access concept
Privileged access is a higher level of permission that lets a user or system make important changes or view sensitive information.
privileges concept
Privileges are permissions that determine what actions a user or process is allowed to perform on a system.
process, file, and network activity concept
This means records of programs running, files being used, and network connections being made on a system.
process[.]to other
process[.]to is a defanged internet domain referenced in security reporting, with the brackets used to prevent accidental clicking.
production wallet job server product
A production wallet job server is a live operational server that runs automated tasks related to cryptocurrency wallets.
Prompt concept
A prompt is the instruction or question a person gives to an AI system to guide its response.
prompt extraction technique
Prompt extraction is an attempt to make an AI system reveal hidden instructions or information from its prompt.
prompt injection technique
Prompt injection is a way of giving an AI system instructions that may make it behave in unintended ways.
also: direct and indirect injection
prompting technique
Prompting is the practice of giving instructions and information to an AI model to guide its response.
prompts concept
Prompts are the instructions or questions a user gives to an AI system to get a response.
proof-of-concept technique
A working demonstration, often a piece of code, that proves a security vulnerability can actually be exploited.
also: PoC
Proof-of-Concept (PoC) Code tool
Proof-of-concept code is example software that demonstrates that a vulnerability can be exploited.
also: POC code
Proof-of-Concept Code concept
Proof-of-concept code is sample code that shows a security flaw can be exploited, often used by researchers and sometimes copied by attackers.
Public disclosure concept
Public disclosure is the act of making information, such as a security flaw, available to the public.
Public exploit code concept
Public exploit code is attack code shared openly that shows how to take advantage of a vulnerability.
public exploits concept
Public exploits are attack code or instructions available to anyone that show how to take advantage of a vulnerability.
Public GitHub Repositories concept
Public GitHub repositories are code projects that anyone on the internet can view and copy.
Public repositories concept
Public repositories are online code storage spaces that anyone can view.
public repository concept
A public repository is an online code or file storage area that anyone can view and sometimes copy from.
Publicly available exploit concept
Attack code that has been released where anyone can obtain and potentially use it.
Publicly disclosed concept
Publicly disclosed means information has been made available for the public to know.
pull request concept
A pull request is a request to review and merge code changes into a shared software project.
pull requests concept
Pull requests are proposals to merge code changes into a software project, commonly used on platforms like GitHub.
also: PR, PRs
Pull-Request Poisoning technique
A supply-chain attack technique that abuses code-review or pull-request processes to get malicious code released.
push technique
A push is the act of sending local code changes to a remote source-code repository such as GitHub.
Push Security organization
Push Security is a cybersecurity company focused on protecting identity, SaaS, and browser-based employee activity.
Python tool
Python is a popular programming language often used to write scripts, automation tools, and security research code.
QEMU tool
QEMU is an open-source emulator and virtualization tool used to run operating systems or software in virtual machines.
Quad9 organization
A public DNS resolver service that can block access to many known malicious domains.
Queries concept
Requests sent to a database to retrieve, add, change, or remove information.
Quick Assist tool
Quick Assist is a Microsoft remote support tool that lets one person view or control another Windows computer with permission.
race condition vulnerability
A race condition is a bug where software behaves unpredictably because two operations happen in an unexpected order or at the same time.
ransom payments concept
Ransom payments are money paid to criminals in hopes of recovering data, stopping leaks, or restoring access after an attack.
ransomware concept
Ransomware is malicious software or an operation that locks or steals data to pressure victims into paying money.
ransomware activity concept
Ransomware activity is behavior related to malware that locks or steals data and demands payment from victims.
ransomware groups threat-actor
Ransomware groups are criminal teams that use ransomware or data theft to extort victims for money.
Ransomware leak sites concept
Ransomware leak sites are websites where extortion groups publish stolen victim data to pressure organizations into paying.
RAR archive concept
A RAR archive is a compressed file package that can bundle one or more files together, sometimes used to hide or deliver malware.
RAT malware
A RAT, or remote access trojan, is malware that lets an attacker remotely control an infected device.
RC4 protocol
RC4 is an older encryption method that was once widely used but is now considered unsafe for protecting sensitive data.
Real time concept
Real time means something happens or is shown immediately, or with very little delay.
real-time container events concept
These are live notifications about actions and status changes involving containers, such as starting or stopping.
real-world attacks concept
Real-world attacks are actual attempts to break into, damage, or abuse systems outside of a lab or classroom setting.
Reasoning concept
Reasoning is the process of working through information logically to reach an answer or decision.
reassembly technique
Reassembly is the process of combining separate pieces of data or network packets into their original complete form.
reconnaissance technique
Reconnaissance is the information-gathering step attackers use to learn about a target before trying to break in.
Recover concept
Recover means restoring systems and business operations after a cyber incident.
recovery bounty program concept
A recovery bounty program offers rewards to people or organizations that help locate, freeze, or return stolen assets.
Reddit product
Reddit is an online platform where users post and discuss content in communities.
RedFlick technique
RedFlick is a malware-delivery method associated with the Callisto threat actor.
redirect concept
A redirect sends a browser or request from one web address to another.
redirects concept
Redirects are instructions that automatically send a user or browser from one web address to another.
Redundant, Obsolete, and Trivial concept
A category of data, often called ROT data, that is duplicated, outdated, or no longer useful.
also: ROT
refresh token concept
A refresh token is a login token that lets an app get new access tokens without making the user sign in again.
Registration Changes concept
Updates to a domain's ownership, contact, or registration details.
Registry concept
The Registry is a Windows database that stores system and application settings.
regulated data concept
Information subject to legal or industry rules about how it must be stored, processed, or shared.
relay concept
A relay is a server or service that forwards network traffic or email from one place to another.
release assets concept
Release assets are downloadable files attached to a software release, such as installers, archives, or documentation.
Release Automation concept
The use of automated systems to build, test, package, and publish software releases.
also: publisher workflow, publishing process, release workflow
Release Tags concept
Release tags are version labels that point to specific code releases so users can select a version to run.
Remediation actions concept
Remediation actions are steps taken to fix or reduce a security problem, such as patching, changing settings, or removing malware.
remote access concept
The ability to connect to another computer or network from a distant location and use it as if you were physically present.
remote access client tool
A remote access client is software that lets someone connect to and control another computer over a network.
remote access software concept
Software that allows a user to control a computer from a remote location, often abused by scammers and attackers to gain unauthorized access.
remote access tooling tool
Software that lets someone connect to and control a computer from another location.
Remote access tools tool
Remote access tools let someone control or manage a computer from another location, which can be legitimate or abused by attackers.
remote access trojan malware
A remote access trojan is malware that secretly lets an attacker control a victim's computer from somewhere else.
remote attacker concept
A remote attacker is someone who tries to exploit a system over a network without needing physical access to it.
remote control technique
Remote control means operating a computer, phone, or system from another location over a network.
Remote Desktop Sessions protocol
Active connections that let a person control or use another computer from a distance.
Remote management concept
Remote management is controlling or configuring a computer, server, or device from another location over a network.
Remote management software tool
Remote management software lets someone administer or control a computer over a network.
remote management tools tool
Remote management tools let administrators control, monitor, or fix computers from another location, but attackers can also abuse them.
Remote monitoring and management tool
Remote monitoring and management is software that lets IT staff watch and control computers or networks from afar.
remote payload concept
A remote payload is malicious or functional code downloaded from another server instead of being included locally.
Remote Support product
Remote Support is software or a service that lets a technician connect to a user’s device from another location to help fix problems.
remote support tooling tool
Software designed to let support staff remotely view, troubleshoot, or control another computer.
also: remote support utilities, remote-support tools
remote-code-execution technique
Remote code execution is a serious flaw that lets an attacker run commands on a system from elsewhere.
Remotely tool
Remotely is a remote administration tool that can be used to access and manage computers over a network.
Remus malware
An information-stealing malware family that collects data such as credentials from infected devices.
Replayed technique
Replayed means captured data, such as a token or request, is sent again to try to repeat an action or gain access.
repos concept
Repos are repositories, meaning storage locations for source code, project files, or software packages.
repositories concept
Repositories are places where software project files and related development data are stored.
repository concept
A repository is a storage location for code, files, and their change history, especially in systems like GitHub.
Reproducer concept
A small example or test program created to reliably demonstrate a software bug or security issue.
also: technical reproduction note
research concept
Research means systematically looking for information, testing ideas, or studying a topic to learn more about it.
also: study, findings
researchers organization
Researchers are people who study systems, threats, or vulnerabilities to understand and improve security.
residential dynamic broadband address concept
A residential dynamic broadband address is an IP address assigned temporarily to a home internet customer.
resilience concept
The ability of an organization to anticipate, withstand, and recover from adverse cyber events and security breaches.
Respond technique
Respond means to take action after detecting a security issue, such as containing an attack or fixing affected systems.
Restart concept
A restart is turning a device or program off and then back on again to refresh it or apply changes.
Restore technique
Restore means to bring data, settings, or a system back to an earlier working state.
Retrieval-Augmented Generation technique
A technique where an AI model first retrieves relevant facts from a database and then uses them when generating an answer, reducing mistakes.
also: RAG
reverse engineering technique
Reverse engineering is taking software apart to understand how it works without relying on the original source code.
Reverse Shells technique
A remote command connection in which an infected computer calls back to an attacker's system for instructions.
revocation concept
The process of invalidating a digital credential or certificate so it can no longer be used.
risk-based policies concept
Security rules that change or restrict access when a login or activity appears risky.
RMM tool
Software tools used by IT teams to manage computers remotely, sometimes abused by attackers to maintain persistent control over infected machines.
RMM tools tool
RMM tools are remote monitoring and management programs that let administrators manage computers from elsewhere.
root access concept
Having complete administrative control over a computer or network, allowing unrestricted system changes.
root privileges concept
Root privileges are the highest level of control on Unix-like systems, allowing a user or program to change almost anything.
root-level concept
Root-level means having the highest level of control over a device or operating system.
root-level access concept
Root-level access is the highest level of control on many systems, allowing someone to change almost anything.
Root-Level Privileges concept
The highest level of access on a computer, allowing someone to control nearly all system settings and files.
Router concept
In a mixture-of-experts AI model, a router chooses which specialized components should process each input.
router firmware product
Router firmware is the built-in software that controls how a router operates.
RouterOS product
RouterOS is MikroTik's operating system for routers, used to manage networking, firewall, wireless, and routing features.
RouterOS 7 product
RouterOS 7 is a major version of MikroTik's RouterOS operating system for routers and network devices.
routers product
Routers are network devices that send internet traffic between your home, office, or other networks and the wider internet.
run code concept
To run code means to make a computer execute instructions written in a programming language.
RunFile tool
A ScreenConnect feature that can run a file or command on a remotely managed computer.
RunOnce technique
A Windows registry key that lists programs to be run once at the next user login, commonly abused by malware for persistence.
RunPE technique
A malware technique that starts a program by placing its code inside another process's memory and redirecting execution to it.
russia
Russia is a country frequently referenced in cybersecurity stories involving cybercrime groups, espionage, and government activity.
Russia-aligned group threat-actor
A Russia-aligned group is a threat actor or hacking group believed to support, work from, or share interests with Russia.
Russia-linked threat-actor
A description for threat actors or activity reported as having connections to Russia.
Russia-linked hackers threat-actor
Russia-linked hackers are threat actors believed to have ties to Russia through location, sponsorship, tasking, or shared interests.
Russian government organization
The Russian government is Russia's national governing organization and is often mentioned in cyber and geopolitical reporting.
Russian hackers threat-actor
Russian hackers are cyber attackers or groups described as operating from Russia or being linked to Russian interests.
Rust tool
Rust is a programming language often used to build fast and memory-safe software, including security tools and malware.
SaaS controls concept
Security settings and protections used to manage access to cloud-based software services.
SABC News organization
A news service operated by the South African Broadcasting Corporation.
Safari product
Apple's web browser that comes pre-installed on Macs, iPhones, and iPads.
also: Safari browser
safeguards concept
Safeguards are protections put in place to reduce the chance or impact of harm, misuse, or security incidents.
sailpoint
SailPoint is an identity security company that helps organizations manage who has access to systems and data.
sanctioned concept
Sanctioned means officially restricted or penalized by a government, often by banning business dealings or freezing assets.
sanctions concept
Government-imposed restrictions that block or limit trade, financial dealings, or travel with targeted individuals or countries.
sandbox concept
A sandbox is an isolated environment used to run code more safely so it cannot easily affect the rest of the system.
sandboxing technique
Sandboxing means running a file or program in an isolated environment so it can be observed safely without risking the real system.
Scam technique
A scam is a dishonest scheme designed to trick people into giving up money, information, or access.
Scam messages concept
Scam messages are texts, emails, or chats designed to trick people into sending money, data, or access.
scam pages technique
Web pages made to deceive visitors into giving money, passwords, or personal information.
scams concept
Scams are dishonest schemes designed to trick people into giving money, information, or access.
Scan Fingerprint concept
A set of technical traits collected during a scan that helps identify or compare an internet-facing service.
scanning technique
Scanning is checking computers, networks, or services to find what is reachable and what may be vulnerable.
Scanning tools tool
Scanning tools are programs that check systems or networks for exposed services, weaknesses, or signs of compromise.
scans concept
Scans are automated checks that examine software or related data for issues or information.
scheduled-tasks
Scheduled tasks are automated jobs on a computer that attackers can abuse to run malware at specific times or after reboot.
SCL=-1 concept
SCL=-1 is a Microsoft email spam score value that usually means a message is treated as trusted and bypasses normal spam filtering.
scope concept
scope defines what access, targets, or permissions are included in a security test, login request, or authorization grant.
scratch buffer concept
A scratch buffer is a temporary area of computer memory used while a program processes data.
screen recordings concept
Screen recordings are videos that capture what is displayed and done on a computer screen.
screenconnect
ScreenConnect, now ConnectWise Control, is a remote-support tool that attackers sometimes abuse for unauthorized access.
screenshots concept
Images that capture what is currently shown on a computer screen.
script injection technique
Script injection is an attack where unwanted code is inserted into a web page or application so it runs in someone’s browser.
SD-WAN concept
SD-WAN is software-defined wide-area networking, a way to manage business network connections using centralized software controls.
SD-WAN vManage product
Cisco's management platform for configuring and monitoring SD-WAN networks.
second stage technique
A second stage is follow-up malware or code that is downloaded or run after an initial infection succeeds.
Secondary payloads concept
Secondary payloads are additional pieces of malware or code delivered after an initial infection to expand what the attacker can do.
Security incident concept
A security incident is an event where systems, data, or accounts may have been attacked, exposed, or misused.
security leaders concept
Security leaders are people responsible for guiding an organization’s cybersecurity strategy and teams.
security patch concept
A security patch is a software update that fixes a vulnerability or weakness attackers could exploit.
security products concept
Software or hardware designed to protect systems from cyber threats, like antivirus or firewalls.
security professionals concept
Security professionals are people whose job is to protect systems, data, and organizations from security threats.
Security relevant concept
Security relevant means important to protecting systems or understanding risk.
Security team organization
A security team is the group of people responsible for protecting an organization's systems and data.
security teams concept
Groups of professionals responsible for protecting an organization's information, systems, and networks from cyber threats.
security tools tool
Security tools are software or hardware products used to detect, prevent, investigate, or respond to cyber threats.
security updates concept
Security updates are software fixes that close vulnerabilities or improve protection against threats.
Security vulnerabilities vulnerability
Security vulnerabilities are weaknesses in software, hardware, or processes that attackers can exploit.
segmentation technique
Segmentation is dividing a network or system into separate parts to limit how far an attacker can move.
self-hosted concept
Self-hosted means an organization runs software on servers it controls instead of using a vendor's cloud service.
send.php tool
A PHP script that sends data submitted through a website form to other systems.
sender concept
A sender is the person, account, server, or system that sends a message such as an email.
Sender Spoofing technique
A technique that makes an email appear to have been sent by a different person or organization.
also: spoofed sender identities, spoofed email
Sensitive and Regulated Data concept
Information that needs extra protection because it is private, valuable, or covered by laws and regulations.
sensitive data concept
Sensitive data is information that could cause harm if exposed, such as passwords, financial details, or medical records.
sensitive information concept
Sensitive information is data that should be protected because exposing it could harm a person, company, or system.
Sensitive personal information concept
Sensitive personal information is private data, such as identity, health, financial, or contact details, that could harm someone if exposed.
serialized concept
Serialized means data has been converted into a storable or transferable format that software can later reconstruct.
service accounts concept
Service accounts are accounts used by software or systems rather than by individual people.
serviceproxy-access.log tool
A log file that records requests handled by a service proxy.
session hijacking technique
Session hijacking is when an attacker steals or takes over a user’s logged-in web session so they can act as that user.
session tokens concept
Session tokens are temporary digital values that prove a user is already logged in to a website or service.
severity concept
Severity is a rating that describes how serious a security issue is.
SFV:SKN concept
SFV:SKN is an email filtering status that indicates spam filtering was skipped because a message was previously treated as non-spam.
SHA-256 concept
SHA-256 is a hashing method that creates a fixed-size digital fingerprint of data.
SHA-256 hash concept
A SHA-256 hash is a fixed-length digital fingerprint used to identify data or files.
sharepoint
SharePoint is Microsoft’s platform for storing, sharing, and collaborating on documents and internal websites.
shellcode technique
Shellcode is small code used in exploits to make a vulnerable program run attacker-controlled commands.
sideload technique
To sideload an app means installing it from outside the official app store.
signature-based detection technique
Signature-based detection finds threats by matching files, emails, or activity against known patterns of bad behavior or malware.
signup concept
Signup is the process of creating an account, which attackers may abuse with fake identities or automated registrations.
silent-push organization
Silent Push is a threat intelligence company that tracks internet infrastructure used by attackers.
SIM cards product
SIM cards are small chips that identify a mobile phone account to a cellular network.
Simulations concept
Simulations are practice scenarios that imitate real events so people or systems can test how they would respond.
Single Sign On concept
Single Sign On lets a person log in once and then access multiple approved apps without signing in again each time.
SLAPSHOT tool
An attacker tool that forwards network traffic through a compromised system into an internal network.
SlowMist organization
A cybersecurity company that specializes in blockchain and cryptocurrency security investigations.
smartphones product
Smartphones are mobile phones that can run apps, browse the web, and store personal data.
also: smartphone
SMTP protocol
SMTP is the standard internet protocol used to send email between mail servers.
Sneaky 2FA tool
Sneaky 2FA is a named phishing kit or tool referenced in security reporting for bypassing or stealing two-factor authentication flows.
SNMP protocol
SNMP is a protocol used to monitor and manage network devices such as routers, switches, and servers.
SNMP notifications protocol
SNMP notifications are alerts sent by network devices to report status changes, failures, or other events to monitoring systems.
SNOWLIGHT malware
SNOWLIGHT is a named malware family or tool referenced in security reporting.
social engineering technique
Social engineering is manipulation of people into doing something or sharing information they otherwise would not.
social engineering tactics technique
Social engineering tactics are tricks that manipulate people into revealing information or taking unsafe actions.
socket organization
Socket is a software supply-chain security company that scans open-source packages for risky behavior.
software dependencies concept
Software dependencies are outside libraries or components that an application needs in order to work.
Software flaws vulnerability
Software flaws are mistakes or weaknesses in programs that can cause bugs or create security risks.
software updates concept
Software updates are new versions or fixes released to improve features, repair bugs, or close security holes.
software vulnerability vulnerability
A software vulnerability is a flaw in code that attackers may be able to exploit.
Sophisticated Exploits concept
Advanced methods or code that attackers use to take advantage of a software weakness.
South African Government organization
The national government of South Africa.
south-africa other
South Africa is a country that may be mentioned as a location or target in a security story.
spam bombing technique
Sending a large number of unwanted messages to overwhelm a person's inbox or distract them from an attack.
SparkRAT malware

spear-phishing technique
